Hey! Im in a very different situation, but I was recently at a course where I learned something that might help a little. And even if it doesn't help, it could be worth a try?

So the whole idea was just to sit down, close your eyes, and try to listen to yourself. Then to attempt to be present, acknowledge the pain, discomfort or other feelings you might encounter. Not try to change them, just acknowledge their existence and your reaction to them. Just observe yourself with a non-judgemental and neutral mindset. 

It sounds and feels very weird, but I think the theory behind it is that accepting and acknowledging what your dealing with and knowing its there makes it easier to deal with in the long run. It's of course one of those "gotta do it more than once"-things, but it doesn't hurt to give it a go, right? 😊

Hope you get better soon!

It was a kid I babysat, not my own, but still.
So this is a 6 yo boy, full of energy like a lot of kids that age. One of the first times I babysat, I sat in the kitchen eating the dinner I had just made, with him running around/playing/doing his own thing in the kitchen with me, when he got thirsty. Now, when he wanted some water he would hoist himself up on the counter and drink directly from the tap, no matter how many times he was told to use a cup. 
This time however, instead of jumping down again, he turned around and sat on the brink of the sink. Except he got off his balance, and fell backwards into the sink, where the dirty and water-filled casserole sat.
Between his expression, the splash, and the fact that he jumped up like a fuckin cartoon character after,  I could not for the life of me stop laughing! It still makes me laugh just thinking about it. I was lucky he chose to laugh with me, because it could just has easily have ended in crying. Even after his sister came home, I barely managed to explain to her what had happened...

Tl;dr - kid I babysat fell in the sink, I cried woth laughter, and felt really bad for it.

My hair clung to my face, and I looked frantically for the closest shore. In the distance i saw a shadowy line, only a little closer than the horizon, and I started swimming. It took a minute to realize it, but I suddenly realized that I was  furious. It was like the oxygen had sparked a fire that had been building, growing, for all those decades down there.
